edits.finding: round2 decision 1 (FMCW dwell, ungated central case)
edits.old: At 200 m, eye safety therefore binds FMCW point rate only near 25 Mpts/s: the §C7a model's FMCW needs 3.0 W of useful light at 10 Mpts/s and 7.6 W at 25 Mpts/s, within the 9.1 W allowance, but an ungated transmitter, which also emits during the round trips, sends 8.6–9.6 W at 25 Mpts/s and reaches it (§C7a(b); §C7b subsection 2(i)). Below that, heat and wall-plug efficiency (optical output power per unit of electrical input power) bind first (§C7a). At 300 m and 25 Mpts/s, however, the model's 11 W would exceed the allowance for this field (§C7b subsection 2(i)).
edits.new: At 200 m, eye safety therefore binds FMCW point rate only near 25 Mpts/s. The §C7a model's FMCW needs 3.0 W of useful light at 10 Mpts/s and 7.6 W at 25 Mpts/s. Its central case is ungated, so the laser also emits during the round trips: $T_{\rm dwell}/T_{\rm int}=12.67\ \mu{\rm s}/10\ \mu{\rm s}=1.27$ times as much, where $T_{\rm int}$ is the useful up- plus down-chirp ($2\times5\ \mu{\rm s}$) and $T_{\rm dwell}=T_{\rm int}+2\tau$ adds two round trips of $\tau=2R/c=1.33$ µs (§C7b Eq. (107)). That is ≈3.8 W at 10 Mpts/s, within the 9.1 W allowance, and ≈9.6 W at 25 Mpts/s, just above it; a transmitter gated during the round trips would emit only the 7.6 W of useful light and stay within it (§C7a(b); §C7b subsection 2(i)). Below 25 Mpts/s, heat and wall-plug efficiency (optical output power per unit of electrical input power) bind first (§C7a). At 300 m and 25 Mpts/s even the useful light, the model's 11 W, would exceed the allowance for this field (§C7b subsection 2(i)).
edits.why: The §C7a central case is ungated (T_dwell = T_int + 2 tau): emitted power 3.84 / 9.61 W at 10 / 25 Mpts/s.

$\Omega_{\rm pix}=(0.05°\times\pi/180)^2=(8.73\times10^{-4})^2=7.62\times10^{-7}$ sr.
- **Worked example, 940 nm.** $L=0.9\times1.43\times10^{18}/\pi=4.11\times10^{17}\ {\rm s^{-1}\,m^{-2}\,sr^{-1}\,nm^{-1}}$, so Eq. (67) gives $r_{\rm bg}=4.11\times10^{17}\times10\times4.91\times10^{-4}\times7.62\times10^{-7}\times0.5\times0.37=2.8\times10^{8}$ counts/s. - **Basis against §C6(d).** A band average is what a filter integrates, and at 940 nm the ±10 nm average used here, 0.303 W m⁻² nm⁻¹, is $0.472/0.303=1.56$ times below the exact-wavelength value and $0.39/0.303=1.29$ times below the 0.39 that §C6(d) and the §C7a ToF model take (the midpoint of the two; at 905 nm $0.75/0.693=1.08$), so the model's 940 nm background is about 1.3× this table's and the model is conservative for 940 nm ToF.
